Signals to watch: peer-reviewed PCM cells demonstrations, array logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting drift compensation uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Phase-Change Memory Arrays Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Phase-Change Memory Arrays: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Phase-Change Memory Arrays — memory that computes where it stores.

Phase 1 — Prove (PCM cells): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (array logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (drift compensation): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (multilevel cells): array hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and datacenters-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
